title: How Glory Goes still one of the greatest songs ever written though #f...
transcript: Floyd Collins absolutely broke my heart and not in the way that it was supposed to unfortunately and this musical follows the true story of Floyd Collins who 100 years ago got trapped in a cave and there were so many efforts to get him out of this cave that a media frenzy formed it is actually considered one of the first viral moments in broadcast media history that wasn't related to a war that's how big this was when it happened and I've been really excited for this musical because I have been listening to the cast recording of the original off Broadway production for literal decades at this point literal decades I love this score so much but I should have known that there was a reason that people just don't do the show all the time and here I foolishly thought I was probably because it's a really dark subject matter like parade like people are performing parade everywhere because it's kind of a depressing show but it turns out that people don't often produce the show because while the score is lovely the book is kind of a train wreck because one of the things that I always find so fascinating about the score and this overall story that keeps me drawn to listening to the show other than the absolutely gorgeous melodies by Adam Guettel is this idea of like Floyd Collins going into this cave to make it a tourist destination like the the opening songs that he sings are literally about all the things that he wants to do to this cave to make it a place where like families come and hang out what ends up happening is he essentially becomes the tourist destination people come to the cave because he's in there and they're fascinated by that and that has always been such an interesting story to tell to me and there's parts of that that it feels like it's talking about in the score but the book unfortunately spends so much time on his family and all of the different ways that they tried to get him out of this cave that it doesn't really explore that at all and it ends up kind of becoming this really long drawn out convoluted mess staging of this production also felt really disjointed at times there were there were aspects of it that I genuinely loved like the entire sequence of Floyd Collins exploring the cave at the top of the show I thought was done incredibly creatively and well for the space I do agree with some people I think that Vivian Beaumont's a little too large for this kind of show but I think for the space that they were given they use parts of it very well at times then when we go to the above ground a lot of the transitions didn't make sense to me a lot of the characterizations didn't make sense to me it just I felt like this musical as a whole didn't really understand what story it was trying to tell which is just so frustrating for me because going into this having listened to the score for years I felt like I knew at least from the score what musical it was trying to tell like I feel like those bones are really good and then the rest of it just doesn't live up to it as far as a production as a whole I think you know there are parts of it that work for me parts of it that don't aspects of the design I really liked especially the lighting design the scenic design again is very simple but I thought for the use of space and for everything that it needs to showcase that it was done creatively the performances are kind of hit or miss for me and I think that's a given if from the book itself you don't really understand what story is is being told then how as a performer do you understand how to tell that story right but there are some incredible performances in this and one of them is definitely Jeremy Jordan as Floyd Collins I could have watched him just climb through that cave and yodle to the gods for two two hours and would have been a lot happier in fact if I have one other complaint it's that there's not enough Jeremy Jordan in this because we spend so much time above ground without him we also get an incredible performance by Taylor Trensch as Skeets Miller who's the first journalist to arrive on the scene and start reporting on Floyd Collins and Jason Gotay as Homer Collins gives an incredible rendition of Day Break just stunning I cannot wait for this cast recording at the end of the day I'm so happy I finally got to see a production of this show and to hear this score be sung on a stage and again I am so elated that we are getting an updated cast recording and I will in fact be going to see this again next week with my mother who introduced me to this cast recording and I'm really glad that we get to experience this together I just I so wish this was a better show overall like give me two hours with that book and the more I think about it the more that I think that Dead Outlaw actually tells the story closer to what I was expecting from Floyd Collins than I actually got out of Floyd Collins as far as tickets go I got mine through the lottery and it was the best lottery ticket I've ever gotten it was literally dead centre orchestra next week I will be sitting in the linctix section which is all the way to the side and I'm very curious what some of the visuals look like from the side seats I will be opposite of the chair section where Floyd Collins spends most of the show uh so there won't be any sightline issues I know that if you're sitting far house left if you're super close to the stage there can be some sideline issues where Floyd Collins sitting in his chair is kind of blocking some of your view of the rest of the show definitely be aware of that linctix are also sold out for this production I do believe but there is in addition to the lottery a student rush that Lincoln Center offers for all of their productions with an ID
reasoning: The reviewer expresses deep frustration with the show's book and staging despite loving the score for decades, calling it a 'train wreck' and 'convoluted mess.' However, she praises individual performances (especially Jeremy Jordan) and is seeing it again, indicating mixed feelings rather than discouragement.
